thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: CeresCorp (dedicated pool ceres-prod-2) - elevated error rate + logs containing raw request bodies (possible PII). Pager oncall: @olivia.

olivia: ack. I'm on it, looking at metrics and logs now.

matt: taking signal collection. any idea impact surface?

olivia: initial spike at 23:04 UTC, 5xxs from model proxy. I can see repeated request dumps in stdout that include full user payloads. Looks like a logging toggle flip during recent deploy.

angela: @olivia any customer-visible outages? CeresCorp is an enterprise VPC customer on Dedicated capacity.

olivia: no request failures reported to client yet, but logs with payloads were shipped to central ELK for ~7 minutes. We need to stop log shipping and assess retention/exports.

incident-bot: ACTION REQUIRED: disable central log forwarding for ceres-prod-2, collect minimal evidence, notify security and legal.

olivia: I'm going to take the quick mitigation path: disable log-forwarder on that pool and flip log level to error. @matt handing over to you for forensic artifacts and scrub.

matt: on it. pulling the bucket listing and tail of the shipper. running safe grep to enumerate potentially sensitive keys.

matt: command I'm running: 
```
kubectl -n ded ceres-prod-2 logs -l app=log-forwarder --since=10m | head -n 200 > /tmp/ceres_raw_samples.log
```

matt: found ~120 entries containing keys: email, ssn, phone_number, credit_card. Sample shows raw request JSON.

jordan: tagging sec. We need to know if any logs were exported to third-party (S3, external ES). If yes, stop outgoing replication and start preservation hold.

ops-bot: Replication check: recent exports to s3://redwood-exports/cerescorp/ at 2026-06-18T23:06Z. 3 objects (logs-20260618-2306.gz).

kevin: legal on call. We need minimal access policy for forensic team. No copies shared outside Redwood legal+sec+oncall+customer-ops+AE. Any extracts shared to customer must be redacted or via secure upload.

sam: I'll prep a short note to CeresCorp. We need to be transparent but controlled. Suggest: "We're investigating a logging configuration issue that may have temporarily captured payloads; we are containing and will coordinate next steps with you."

angela: Can we produce a scrubbed artifact for the customer showing request ids and timestamps but no PII?

matt: yes — plan: create a redaction pipeline using jq + sed to mask emails/SSNs before producing viewable artifacts. Example scrub script: 
```
cat /tmp/ceres_raw_samples.log | 
jq -r '. | @json' | 
sed -E 's/\"([A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+)@([A-Za-z0-9.-]+)\"/"REDACTED_EMAIL"/g; s/([0-9]{3}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{4})/REDACTED_SSN/g' > /tmp/ceres_samples_scrubbed.log
```

jordan: good. Also add a pipeline rule to mask at ingest to prevent future leak. Rule: drop request_body or replace with hash for production logs.

olivia: Mitigation steps I'm executing now: (1) disable forwarder pods on ceres-prod-2 (kubectl scale --replicas=0 deployment/log-forwarder) (2) set service log_level=error (3) add temporary ES index write-block for ceres prefix.

incident-bot: Runbook checkpoint: set retention hold? required for legal preservation? Reply with `preserve` to confirm.

kevin: preserve. Legal requests preservation of exports and immutable copies; preserve in locked S3 path and create access log.

matt: I've copied the 3 exported objects to s3://legal-hold/cerescorp/20260618/ and set object lock. checksum: sha256:5d9f...

angela: Who will own the customer communication? @sam please coordinate with support for exact wording and timeline.

sam: I'll take it. Draft to CeresCorp out in 30m. Will ask for consent before we share scrubbed logs.

olivia: Handoff: I'm wrapping initial containment. Switching to monitoring only. @matt you take incident lead for forensic + scrub. I'll be available if needed. Next oncall: @matt becomes primary.

matt: acknowledged. I'll also create a minimal redaction artifact and run a PII scanner to get counts by type. ETA 45m.

kevin: legal note: no external sharing of raw logs. If the customer requests raw logs for their audit, route through legal and secure transfer with NDA/justification.

angela: ops note: we should consider a feature-flag to prevent logging full request body for Dedicated pools by default. Filing a product ticket.

olivia: filing that ticket now: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENGOPS-4821 

incident-bot: INCIDENT: containment >= done. Severity downgraded to P2. Keep thread updated with artifacts and communications.

matt: attaching scrubbed sample (s3 link, access via secure-token only). Will post counts and redaction log next.

sam: sent customer note (copy to thread). CeresCorp replied: "Appreciate quick action. Please let us know exact fields exposed and retention." Asked for ETA for scrubbed artifact.

matt: sending counts: emails: 87, ssn-like patterns: 3, phone: 42, cards: 0. All artifacts scrubbed and uploaded to legal-hold.

kevin: legal to prepare letter describing retention/mitigation for CeresCorp and internal record.

olivia: thanks team. I'll close out containment checklist and schedule a postmortem with impacted services and product for next week.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: resolved->monitoring. Please file postmortem: tag incident-PII and customer:cerescorp.

angela: noted. I'll draft the customer-facing FAQ for support and sales.

matt: handing off final artifacts to legal and operations. leaving follow-ups in ENGOPS-4821.

olivia: signoff from oncall. End of handoff. :white_check_mark:"
